key_insight: A transition-based digital twin model can better track Alzheimer's progression from sparse, irregular visits than a purely sequence-based approach.
clinical_relevance: This could support more personalized forecasting of cognitive decline and diagnostic changes, with uncertainty-aware what-if scenario analysis for individual patients.
method: Combines multimodal longitudinal data: cognitive tests, clinical variables, and MRI-derived phenotypes
Integrates adjacent-visit transition modelling with sequence-based temporal modelling
Outputs predicted cognitive status, diagnosis, and uncertainty estimates
evidence_signal: On leak-free subject-level ADNI splits, the model showed strong score forecasting and diagnosis classification, with adjacent-visit transition modelling outperforming the sequence branch in this sparse setting.
watch_item: Results come from ADNI retrospective data, so real-world generalization and clinical workflow usefulness still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Transition-Based Digital Twin Modelling for Alzheimer's Disease under Sparse Longitudinal Data
